newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wesfarmers eyes Dampier pipeline buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wesfarmers eyes Dampier pipeline buy.

text.p: Wesfarmers Ltd said on Tuesday it was in talks with possible joint venture partners for a bid to purchase the Western Australian government's Dampier gas pipeline.
The state government has said the pipeline would be sold for between A$600 million and up to A$1 billion.
Western Australian Minister Colin Barnett announced in August that the government would sell the Dampier to Bunbury pipeline, which had a book value of A$1 billion, over the next 18 months.
The 1,540 km pipeline transports gas from the North West Shelf gas project to Perth and southwestern Australia.

"We are likely to be involved in the evaluation of the sale of the Dampier to South West pipeline which is going to take place in the next year or so," Wesfarmers chief executive Michael Chaney told a Securities Institute briefing in Sydney.
"We are currently talking to potential partners on that," he said.

Chaney later told reporters that Perth-based Wesfarmers would be interested in a stake closer to 50 percent than nought, although this depended on how much of the pipeline is sold. "The government has suggested it might only privatise 60 percent. If it's A$600 million we'd obviously take a bigger interest than if it was bigger (than A$600 million)," he said.
Wesfarmers had been in discussions with lots of overseas companies and some Australian companies as potential partners for any purchase, he said.
Wesfarmers had adequate spare debt facilities to fund such a purchase, given that any bidding vehicle would also be geared.
"It would be quite possible for us to do that," he said, adding that Wesfarmers could borrow about A$200 million given its current net gearing ratio of about 42 percent.
This was well within Wefarmers' target range of 40 to 65 percent.

"If the pipeline was A$600 million and we took 50 percent, that's A$300 million, we'd probably do it through a vehicle which itself was geared, so we might have A$100 million (of equity in), with $200 million of debt in the vehicle," he said.
Wesfarmers shares closed down 15 cents at A$8.50 on Tuesday.
